subject: Multiple imputation via semTools and lavaan

messages.author: 9859632b4d9ea4eb
messages.subject: Multiple imputation via semTools and lavaan
parts:
Greetings all,

I am receiving the following set of warinings after using semTools for multiple imputation 

fitmi <- sem.mi(pathmodel,data=scimodel,m=5,seed=12345,miPackage="Amelia",chi="mplus")
Warning messages:
1: In estimateVCOV(lavaanModel, samplestats = lavaanSampleStats, options = lavaanOptions,  :
  lavaan WARNING: could not compute standard errors!

There are, in fact, 10 of these warnings.  I also receive the following error after the output.  

Because the original method to find the baseline model does not work, 
please do not use any fit measures relying on baseline model, including CFI and TLI. 
To find the correct one, please use the inspect function: inspect(object, what='fit').

Using the "inspect" procedure does give me complete set of fit indices.  

tWhen I use FIML to handle missing data within lavaan and not through semTools, it runs fine with no errors.  Any thoughts?

Thanks in advance,

David

messages.author: 5d4f9e7f97c21008
messages.subject: Re: Multiple imputation via semTools and lavaan
parts:
Hi David,

This happens on occasion. When using either the Mplus or MR method of combining chi square statistics (they are identical) six models are fit to each imputed data set (the hypothesized model, the null model, the saturated model, and three models with fixed parameters). Pinpointing where the errors pop up is the fun part. So here come the (first set) of questions:

1. Did sem.mi give you (reasonable) parameter estimates and SEs? If so then the problem isn't in the hypothesized model.
2. If you run the same code but change the chi option to 'lmrr' do you get the same errors?

I need to do a bit of digging to look into the "inspect" issue (providing fit indices there but not with summary). I know this has popped up before and I can't remember the precise reason.

Lastly, any chance you could post your model and data (or a facsimile of them)? Either here or if you want to email me (schoe...@ecu.edu), it would be really helpful to debug this.

Thanks,

Alex

messages.author: 5d4f9e7f97c21008
messages.subject: Re: Multiple imputation via semTools and lavaan
parts:
Hi David,

I found one answer this morning. The message you receive in the output ("Because the original method to find the baseline model does not work, please do not use any fit measures relying on baseline model, including CFI and TLI. To find the correct one, please use the inspect function: inspect(object, what='fit').") is currently a stop gap. We haven't implemented the fit.measures=TRUE option for the summary command when using MI or auxiliary variables (it is on the TODO list). The results in inspect are the complete set of fit indices (though if you set chi to "all" in runMI it provides fit based on the Mplus chi square).

Still not sure about the other warnings, they're probably specific to the data.

Thanks,

Alex
